title: Blending direction, management and agile delivery
blurb: Explain what PRINCE2 Agile is: PRINCE2 direction and management blended with agile product delivery, with governance and control throughout.
question: Why does PRINCE2 Agile combine PRINCE2 Project Management with agile, rather than using either one on its own?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile looks at a project in three areas: project direction, project management and product delivery. Project management methods are strong in governance and control but give little focus to product delivery. Agile is strong in product delivery and responding to change but says relatively little about direction and management. PRINCE2 Agile covers all three, keeping governance and control throughout.

teach.caption: PRINCE2 Agile takes the strength of each (3.1).

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile is PRINCE2 Project Management (its principles, practices and processes) tailored with the agile mindset, agile frameworks, artifacts, techniques and workshops. It is designed for projects using iterative and incremental delivery. It is not a replacement for PRINCE2 and not just Scrum with reports: it blends the two so governance and agile delivery support each other.

head: Area
Typical roles
Typical agile artifacts

teach.body: The book recognizes that some organizations choose not to use agile delivery at all and adopt PRINCE2 Project Management only for overall governance and control, because they feel agile does not suit their needs. PRINCE2 Agile is the choice when the delivery is iterative and incremental and the organization wants governance around it.

Thornbury College is replacing its student portal. The board, led by executive Priya Natarajan, authorizes stages and sets tolerances (direction). Project manager Callum Reid keeps the release map and project dashboard up to date (management). Two Scrum-style teams, each with a product owner, build the portal in two-week iterations (delivery). The board gets control without telling teams how to work; the teams get freedom without losing sight of the business case.

teach.text: Classic wrong ideas: 'PRINCE2 Agile replaces PRINCE2', 'agile handles direction well on its own' and 'project management is strong on product delivery'. The book's view is the reverse: project management is strong on governance and control, agile on product delivery, and PRINCE2 Agile covers all three areas with governance throughout.

items: Three areas: project direction, project management, product delivery (Figure 3.1).
Project management: strong on governance and control, little focus on product delivery.
Agile: strong on product delivery and responding to change, light on direction and management.
PRINCE2 Agile addresses all three with governance and control throughout.

summary: You can now explain PRINCE2 Agile as a blend: PRINCE2 direction and management with agile product delivery. You can also say where each approach is strong and why the combination keeps governance and control throughout.

A.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, where does the main strength of project management lie?
options: In product delivery and responding to change
A.why: The strength of project management lies in governance and control; it gives little focus to product delivery (3.1).

whyNot.0: Product delivery and responding to change are agile's strengths.
whyNot.2: Self-managing teams are an agile feature.
whyNot.3: Iterative team planning comes from agile delivery.

A.q: Which three areas does PRINCE2 Agile address, as shown in Figure 3.1?
options: Project direction, project management, product delivery
Business layer, programme management, project management
Starting up, initiating a project, closing a project
Principles, practices and processes of the method
A.why: Figure 3.1 shows project direction, project management and product delivery; PRINCE2 Agile covers all three (3.1).

whyNot.1: These are organizational levels, not the three areas in Figure 3.1.
whyNot.2: These are three of the seven processes.
whyNot.3: These are three of the five integrated elements.

A.q: Where does agile have relatively little focus, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
A.why: Agile is strong on product delivery and responding to change but has relatively little on project direction and project management (3.1).

whyNot.1: Responding to change is agile's strength.
whyNot.2: Collaboration is a core part of agile working.

B.q: Which statement best describes PRINCE2 Agile?
options: A replacement for PRINCE2 that removes the project board
Scrum with PRINCE2 reports added at the end of each stage
PRINCE2 tailored with agile mindset, frameworks and techniques
A delivery framework designed for single, small agile teams
B.why: PRINCE2 Agile is PRINCE2 Project Management's principles, practices and processes tailored with agile mindset, frameworks, artifacts, techniques and workshops (3.1).

whyNot.0: The board remains; PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance.
whyNot.1: It blends governance and delivery throughout, not reports bolted on.
whyNot.3: It covers direction and management as well, and supports multiple teams.

B.q: An organization uses PRINCE2 Project Management for governance but does not use agile delivery. How does the PRINCE2 Agile book view this?
options: It recognizes some businesses choose this
It says such a project is not really PRINCE2
It says agile delivery must be added later
It treats it as a failed attempt at tailoring
B.why: The book recognizes that some businesses adopt PRINCE2 Project Management only for governance and control, without agile delivery (3.1).

whyNot.1: Using PRINCE2 for governance is still PRINCE2.
whyNot.2: The book accepts that agile may not suit every organization.
whyNot.3: It is presented as a legitimate choice, not a tailoring failure.

B.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, which area do the product owner, team coach, developers and testers mainly work in?
B.why: These roles sit with the delivery teams, building and testing products (product delivery).

whyNot.0: Project direction is the board's area.
whyNot.1: Project management is the project manager's area.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is a role on behalf of the board, not one of the three areas.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Agile is strong on product delivery and responding to change.
2. Project management gives strong focus to product delivery.
3. PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control throughout all three areas.
4. PRINCE2 Agile leaves direction to the delivery teams.
C.why: Agile is strong on delivery and change (1); PRINCE2 Agile covers all three areas with governance and control throughout (3) (3.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: project management gives little focus to product delivery.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: project management is light on delivery, and direction stays with the board.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: direction remains with the project board.

C.q: A board authorizes stages and sets tolerances, while teams plan their own iterations within them. Which statement explains why this blend works?
options: Agile already covers board-level direction well
PRINCE2 is already strong on product delivery
Teams set the tolerances for the board to use
PRINCE2 gives governance; agile gives delivery
C.why: PRINCE2 provides governance and control (direction and management); agile provides strong product delivery. Together they cover all three areas (3.1).

whyNot.0: Agile has relatively little on project direction.
whyNot.1: Project management gives little focus to product delivery.
whyNot.2: Tolerances are set by the level above, starting with the board.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 Agile, all three areas of project direction, project management and product delivery are addressed while taking into account the need for governance and [?] throughout.
C.why: PRINCE2 Agile addresses all three areas while keeping governance and control throughout (3.1).

whyNot.0: Velocity is a team measure, not the paired term with governance.
whyNot.1: Flexibility is agile's contribution, not the paired term with governance.
whyNot.3: Collaboration is an agile mindset trait, not the paired term.

reteach.title: The orchestra
reteach.question: How do direction, management and delivery fit together?

blocks.body: Think of an orchestra. The board of the concert hall decides which concerts happen and the budget (direction). The conductor keeps the performance to plan and time (management). The musicians play, adapting to each other moment by moment (delivery). PRINCE2 is strong on the first two; agile is strong on the third. PRINCE2 Agile brings all three together.

blocks.text: Remember the strengths: project management = governance and control; agile = product delivery and responding to change.

test.why: Project management is strong on governance and control; agile on product delivery and responding to change (3.1).

whyNot.1: Project management gives little focus to product delivery.

test.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile keep from PRINCE2 Project Management?
options: Its reports but not its processes
test.why: PRINCE2 Agile keeps the principles, practices and processes and tailors them with agile ways of working.

whyNot.1: PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental delivery.
whyNot.2: It keeps far more than reports; some reports are even replaced by dashboards.
whyNot.3: The hexagon is Version 1; V2 uses seven aspects.

explain.body: The blend gives teams freedom to deliver in an agile way while the board keeps governance and control throughout.

test.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile keep in place across direction, management and delivery?
options: A fixed set of Scrum events
Detailed task plans from the board
test.why: All three areas are addressed while taking into account the need for governance and control throughout (3.1).

whyNot.0: PRINCE2 Agile works with any agile framework, not just Scrum.
whyNot.1: Detailed task planning is done by delivery teams.
whyNot.3: Projects may have one or many delivery teams.
